- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 10% above recent peak), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 5–8% from next 3 periods to prevent overhang.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 periods, reduce forecast slope by 10–15% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5), avoid long-term trend extrapolation — use 3-period moving average for smoothing.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply downward bias adjustment: subtract 2–4% from forecast for next 5 periods if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
